sources.title: A Repair Café Volunteer Shift
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: At the East Market repair café, volunteers meet at 9 a.m. to prepare shared tools for a free repair session. New volunteers sign up for a shift using the schedule beside the entrance. The shift lead checks each tool and places items that need attention in a labelled tray. If the café runs out of a common part, volunteers record the item and tell the visitor what can be repaired that day. They do not promise a completion time until a technician has inspected the item. At closing, the lead passes on any unfinished requests to the next team. Visitors may wait in the seating area while a repair is in progress.

sources.title: Privacy in a School Library Survey
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: A school committee is asking students how they use the quiet study area in the library. The short survey does not request names, student numbers or contact details. Participation is optional, and students may opt out at any time without giving a reason. Two committee coordinators can read the original responses, which will be kept confidential while the results are reviewed. The final report will combine comments into broad themes and will not quote a response that could identify a student. Teachers will receive the summary after the committee checks it for private details. Students can ask the librarian how the information will be used before they decide whether to take part.

sources.title: Registering for a Class at the Riverside Centre
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: The Riverside Centre opens registration for its spring pottery classes on Monday. Each class meets once a week for six weeks, and the fee includes clay and access to shared tools. New participants should fill in the online form and choose a preferred class time. A confirmation email will arrive within two working days if a place is available. When a class is full, the centre puts applicants on a waiting list in the order their forms were received. Staff contact people on that list if a place opens before the first session. Participants who need step-free access can contact the front desk before registering so staff can confirm which room is suitable.
